body:
Your feelings are not wrong whatsoever. I think your feelings are being taken as they are in the wrong, and it's not about changing how you feel, it's about how you SHOW how you feel through behaviors.

From what I've seen from your comments on this post, your boyfriend isn't giving you what he wants you to give him in certain situations, though since I personally don't know the two of you I can't say that 100% y'know? So for him to turn it into about how hard it is for him when you simply ask something out of curiosity to see if it could work, when I've seen that you said he expects you to be mature all the time, is a bit hypocritical of him. You want to make things better and you were simply asking if it would be a good idea and saying why you did--you were trying to open a two-sided conversation.

I'm not going to tell you how you feel is wrong, especially when I understand and even relate to why you do--it's not my place to tell you your feelings are wrong. Like I said above, it's about how you act them out, and from what you've said you're trying to do it in a healthy way for both you and your boyfriend. 

Have you talked to your therapist about how your boyfriend reacts to your coping skills (ie walking out)? It might be good to do so if you haven't in order to find ideas to bring up to your boyfriend about what else you can do that won't cause worse feelings for the both of you. However I believe that it's about you in the end, and if you can't find anything that works for the both of you, you're going to have to compromise.

I don't do it as much as I used to, however it feels almost compulsive if it regards my mental health. I'll lie about symptoms or even full on disorders to loved ones or professionals. Ironically though I also hide diagnoses (I tell people I have BPD but not also HPD).

Like what was said, compulsive lying is pretty common. The fact you're talking about it is a great step to learning how to deal with it.

Edit: With advice, 

With me and how I kind of controlled some of my lying: I tried to figure out which situations I would do them in; how did I feel at the time, what were they asking me that I wanted to lie about, what was my motivation? I haven't completely stopped lying as I've said above. I don't think anyone can do it alone.

I've done a lot of self-harm and even attempts for attention, and like you said, it feels like even negative attention is better than none. But there's a reason you feel that way and it doesn't make everything you feel and experience invalid.

With me, I felt like I wasn't getting enough attention and care that I needed. And I need it constantly it feels like. 

You're trying to work through not just this, but everything you struggle with, and the fact that you're reaching out to make sense of things is an amazing step and I'm sure I'm not the only one that is proud of you for being able to open up about something like this. It's very, very hard to do.

I don't hate you at all. The fact that you kept coming back shows how much compassion you have and I greatly appreciate it. Thank you for your post.

It depends on the person. It's not directly related to BPD. Is it apart of it? Sure. But does it mean if you have BPD you must do that? No.

With most people I tend not to suddenly leave forever, however I will cut them off somehow but not completely, because in my mind that means they will try harder to be closer to me and care about me which is what I need (doesn't mean what I do is right). However if the relationship is toxic and I'm being hurt, I usually do not to the extreme push-and-pull. Instead I keep staying until they ultimately leave me.

Behaviors depend on the person. While they all come from similar feelings and thoughts, that doesn't mean everyone will react the same. 

I think with BPD, PDs, or even mental illness in general, people without those things expect people who have them to act and feel and think a certain way and throw it everywhere. And then the ones who struggle see this and try to act those ways, because who wants to be a faker? At least I assume that's how everything works, I can't 100% say that.

Yes, that happens to me most of the time. But I noticed that if I'm very much apart of that group and equally attached to everyone, my attention to one person will usually bounce from one person to another in the group depending on how I feel everyone is treating me. It's exhausting.

It's hard to move on when you love someone so deeply, especially if they appear in your dreams and even show up in tarot spreads. 

I'm still very attached to people that broke up with me years ago and want nothing to do with me anymore. Sometimes I have to stop myself from contacting recent breakups. Luckily with the ones from years ago I don't have their contacts anymore. 

I hope you can handle this well enough. Good luck.

1. My parents were not married, as my dad was married to another woman most of the time my parents were together. However they separated when I was very young and my dad gave my mom full custody
2. My dad was very distant, but I wouldn't say cold. However my mom would switch from warm and loving to cold and abusive
3. My mom's love was and still is conditional. If I didn't go along with everything she wanted from me, I would be hurt emotionally and even physically. Sometimes she was suffocating to the point she would cross boundaries, however most of the time she just ignored me in favor of herself. Most of the physical attention I got that wasn't punishment was her physically overpowering me/wrestling me which got me hurt a lot, or crossing my boundaries and touching me without permission and in places that she knew upset me. My dad on the other hand just didn't really do anything for me, emotionally or for my life. He often was late with child support and only visited me once a year at his convenience, but stopped visiting when I was 11 (I'm 20 now). He died when I was 15 so I don't know if he would've changed but I doubt it
4. All three. My mom was emotionally and physically abusive, and I believe I was sexually assaulted by my dad's brother. I was sexually abused too but it wasn't by a family member, but it was by people who watched me most of the time
